channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Report: more than a third of Muslim students experience Islamophobia at UK universities
item.description: The Fosis 'Belonging in Question' report surveyed 715 students at 63 institutions. 38% had experienced Islamophobia, and 68% did not feel able to report it.

item.title: Israeli Heritage Minister Amichai Eliyahu calls Palestinians and Muslims 'camel riders' and 'barbarians'
item.description: The minister used the slurs during a speech in the Knesset on 24 November, in a debate on crime in Arab society in Israel.

item.title: The four Sunni schools of Islamic law: Hanafi, Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali — where they differ
item.description: Sunni Islam has four main schools of jurisprudence (madhhabs): Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali. They agree on creed and fundamentals and differ mainly on secondary (furu') rulings. Uzbekistan and Central Asia follow predominantly the Hanafi school.

item.title: The Uzbek diaspora in the United Kingdom: a small but emerging community
item.description: The Uzbek community in the United Kingdom is a small, young diaspora based mainly in London. According to the 2021 UK Census, 3,810 people born in Uzbekistan were recorded in England and Wales. This article sets out the community's formation — from mid-20th-century Turkestani émigrés to the post-1991 stream of students, professionals and asylum seekers — on the basis of sources.

item.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, at the centre of the deportation battle, leaves the US for Spain
item.description: The Salvadoran man left the United States voluntarily. He had been mistakenly deported in 2025 and later returned under a Supreme Court ruling.

item.title: Selective Service registration in the US: a guide for immigrant families
item.description: Almost all men aged 18–25 living in the US — citizens, green-card holders, refugees, asylees, and many undocumented men too — must register with the Selective Service within 30 days of turning 18. There is currently no active draft — this is only a standby list. Who must register, who is exempt, how to register, and the consequences of not registering. Based on sss.gov and USCIS — not legal advice.

item.title: Uzbekistan recruits medical personnel for German clinics via Globogate, salaries up to €2,500
item.description: The Migration Agency is selecting mid-level medical workers aged 20–36 for employment in Germany. The starting salary is €1,900, rising to €2,500 once qualifications are recognised.

item.title: Central Asia's trade with the Gulf has nearly quadrupled in five years; Uzbekistan leads
item.description: According to a Eurasian Development Bank report, trade turnover reached $3.9 billion in 2025. Uzbekistan accounts for 45 percent of the region's trade with the Gulf.

item.title: European court: returning migrants who came via Belarus is not automatically a rights breach
item.description: The Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights heard three cases against Poland, Latvia and Lithuania. States must first identify and protect vulnerable people.

item.title: Iran flogs singer Parastoo Ahmadi over hijab-free concert
item.description: The singer and four of her team were each given 74 lashes. The punishment was for a December 2024 virtual concert performed without the hijab.

item.title: Greek political refugees in Tashkent: after the Greek Civil War (1949)
item.description: In 1949, after the defeat in the Greek Civil War, the Soviet Union took in thousands of Greek political refugees — the largest group was settled in Tashkent. The formation, life and 1980s repatriation of this community, based on verified facts.

item.title: Zelenskyy confirms a drone strike on a Russian ship in the Gulf of Finland
item.description: The Ukrainian president confirmed responsibility for the attack on the cargo ship Sparta II. The ship's 16-member crew was evacuated.

item.title: Uzbekistan and the UK discuss cooperation on seasonal employment
item.description: On 23 November the Migration Agency and the UK's Fair Work Agency met by video link. The agency said more than 14,000 Uzbeks had been sent to the UK for seasonal work over three years.

item.title: US assistance programs explained: how SNAP, WIC and TANF work
item.description: The three main federal programs for low-income families — SNAP (food assistance), WIC (nutrition for women, infants and children) and TANF (temporary cash assistance) — explained: what each is, who can apply, and the immigrant rules (the five-year bar and the 2026 change to 'public charge').

item.title: How conspiracy theories spread and how to recognize them
item.description: What a conspiracy theory is, how it differs from a real conspiracy, the recurring features that help you recognize one, why people believe them and how social media amplifies them — a media-literacy guide based on verified, academic and international sources.

item.title: Uzbekistan's first Olympics as an independent nation: Lillehammer 1994 and Atlanta 1996
item.description: After independence, Uzbekistan first competed under its own flag at the 1994 Lillehammer Winter Games — where Lina Cheryazova won the country's first-ever gold medal. The history from the founding of the National Olympic Committee to Atlanta 1996, based on verified facts.

item.title: South Korea seeks to more than triple funding for a Koryo-saram museum in Tashkent
item.description: The Overseas Koreans Agency has proposed raising the museum's funding from $1.89m to $6.44m for 2027. The opening is timed to the 90th anniversary of the 1937 deportation.

item.title: Afghanistan's Uzbeks and 2021: the Taliban's return, refugees, and crossings into Uzbekistan
item.description: In August 2021 the Taliban took power. The Uzbek community of northern Afghanistan, the flight of Abdul Rashid Dostum, and the crossing of Afghan military aircraft and soldiers over the Amu Darya to Termez — with verified dates and figures.

item.title: Gaza students head to Ireland after winning a visa battle
item.description: More than 60 scholarship students had their visas refused in July; after a High Court ruling, 48 were approved. Today 20 of them set off for Dublin.

item.title: US family-based immigration: how to petition a relative (Form I-130)
item.description: Which relatives can a US citizen or a green-card holder sponsor? The difference between 'immediate relatives' and the 'family preference' categories (F1–F4), Form I-130, the Visa Bulletin and the waiting rules — a reference guide.

item.title: ICE arrests two passengers at Seattle airport — governor calls it 'out of control'
item.description: Masked agents detained two people before boarding at SeaTac. Washington's governor sharply criticized ICE; DHS called it a targeted operation.

item.title: Tajikistan hosts Putin despite ICC warrant — EU expresses regret
item.description: Vladimir Putin visited Dushanbe on 19–20 November. The EU regretted that Tajikistan failed to execute the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant.

item.title: The establishment of Uzbekistan–Kazakhstan relations (1991–1996): diplomacy between neighbours
item.description: How did Central Asia's two large states establish ties in the early years of independence? The Alma-Ata Protocol, the 1992 diplomatic relations, the 1994 Central Asian Union, and the Karimov–Nazarbayev era — with verified dates.

item.title: US government deported one of its own citizens to Mexico — DoJ admits it in court
item.description: Brian José Morales García, a dual citizen born in Denver, was removed to Mexico in April. On 20 November the DoJ conceded his citizenship in court but asked for the lawsuit to be dismissed.

item.title: Nobel committee chair: excellence alone is not enough — translation and recognition matter
item.description: Anders Olsson, chair of the Nobel Committee for Literature, spoke about literature in less widely known languages and the global recognition of Kazakh writers.

item.title: How the United Nations (UN) works: structure, the Security Council and Uzbekistan's membership
item.description: The UN was founded in 1945 and today unites 193 member states. Here is how the General Assembly, the Security Council, the veto, the Secretary-General and the main agencies work — and how Uzbekistan has taken part since 1992.

item.title: The pillars of Islam and iman: the Five Pillars of Islam and the six articles of faith
item.description: The Five Pillars of Islam (arkan al-Islam) are the five acts of worship prescribed for every Muslim: the shahada, prayer, zakat, fasting and the hajj. The six articles of faith (arkan al-iman) are the foundations of belief: faith in God, the angels, the revealed books, the prophets, the Last Day and the divine decree. This guide explains them from a mainstream Sunni (Hanafi) perspective, respectfully and based solely on reputable sources. This is general information, not a religious ruling or fatwa.

item.title: Bukharan merchants in the Russian Empire: the Siberian «Bukharans» and the caravan trade (16th–20th centuries)
item.description: One of the lesser-known chapters of Uzbek and Central Asian migration is the communities of Bukharan merchants and settlers across the Russian Empire. Called «Bukharans» (bukhartsy) in Russian documents, this group in fact covered merchants from across Turkestan, not only from the city of Bukhara. From the 16th–17th centuries they settled in Western Siberia, drove the caravan trade, and were later absorbed into the Siberian Tatars. This guide draws solely on scholarly sources and treats dates as cautiously as the historians do.

item.title: Fuel station struck in Sanaa as Saudi Arabia downs a drone heading for Riyadh
item.description: The Houthis blamed the Saudi-led coalition for the strike on the capital; the same day the coalition intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone heading toward Riyadh.

item.title: Uzbekistan opens talks to access Australia's labour market
item.description: On 20 November, Tashkent held a first practical round of negotiations by video link with representatives of Australia's Northern Territory; oil and gas was named a priority sector.
